{{short description|American chemist (born 1938)}}
'''Donald A. Tomalia''' (born September 5, 1938) is an American chemist who is known as one of the early discoverers of [[dendrimer]]s.

==Biography==
Tomalia earned an undergraduate degree from the [[University of Michigan]], a master's degree from [[Bucknell University]] and a Ph.D. in physical organic chemistry from [[Michigan State University]]. He worked at [[Dow Chemical]] for many years as a research scientist then moved to the [[Michigan Molecular Institute]] as a Senior Lead Scientist. In 1979, Tomalia first reported on the synthesis<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tomalia |first=D. A. |last2=Baker |first2=H. |last3=Dewald |first3=J. |last4=Hall |first4=M. |last5=Kallos |first5=G. |last6=Martin |first6=S. |last7=Roeck |first7=J. |last8=Ryder |first8=J. |last9=Smith |first9=P. |date=1985-01-01 |title=A New Class of Polymers: Starburst-Dendritic Macromolecules |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/pj198510 |journal=Polymer Journal |language=en |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=117–132 |doi=10.1295/polymj.17.117 |issn=1349-0540|url-access=subscription }}</ref> of [[dendrimer]]s, which have been used in nanotechnology and pharmaceuticals.<ref name="Halford">{{cite journal|last1=Halford|first1=Bethany|title=Dendrimers branch out|journal=[[Chemical & Engineering News]]|date=June 13, 2005|volume=83|issue=24|pages=30–36|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/coverstory/83/8324dendrimers.html|accessdate=February 3, 2017|doi=10.1021/cen-v083n024.p030|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The first dendrimer synthesis was noted by winning the Leonardo da Vinci Prize (Paris, 1996).

In 1990, he joined the [[Michigan Molecular Institute]] (MMI) as Professor and Director of Nanoscale Chemistry &Architecture (1990–1999). In 1992, Tomalia founded his own company, Dendritech. The company was purchased by Dow Chemical a few years later. Tomalia was the scientific director of the Center for Biologic Nanotechnology at the [[University of Michigan Health System|University of Michigan Medical School]]. In 2001, Tomalia started Dendritic NanoTechnologies at [[Central Michigan University]]; Starpharma of Australia provided seed money for the venture and Dow took an equity position a few years later.<ref name="DNT">{{cite journal|last1=McCarthy|first1=Alice A.|title=Dendritic NanoTechnologies, Inc.|journal=Chemistry & Biology|date=May 2005|volume=12|issue=5|pages=499–501|doi=10.1016/j.chembiol.2005.05.006|pmid=15911366|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2010, Tomalia founded NanoSynthons, LLC, in [[Mount Pleasant, Michigan]].<ref name="Profile">{{cite web|title=Donald A. Tomalia|url=https://www.sciencehistory.org/historical-profile/donald-a-tomalia|website=Science History Institute|accessdate=March 21, 2018|language=en|date=2016-06-29}}</ref> In 2016, he was named a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=2016 AAAS Fellows honored for advancing science to serve society|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/2016-aaas-fellows-honored-advancing-science-serve-society|website=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|accessdate=February 2, 2017|language=en|date=November 21, 2016}}</ref> He has been named a [[Thomson Reuters Citation Laureates|Thomson Reuters Citation Laureate]].<ref name="Citation">{{cite web|title=Hall of Citation Laureates|url=http://sciencewatch.com/nobel/hall-citation-laureates|accessdate=February 3, 2017}}</ref>
